extra.message: The public, unauthenticated /api/auth/register endpoint accepts a client-supplied `role` field (RegisterRequest.role) and passes it straight into the new User record (role=req.role). Any anonymous caller can POST {"role": "ops_admin"} to self-register as an ops_admin (or dispatcher) account, gaining full administrative access to jobs, users, webhooks and audit logs.

cwe: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management
CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded, publicly-visible default ("change-me-in-production-32-char-key!!") when the SECRET_KEY environment variable is unset. This value is used to sign/verify every JWT (create_access_token/decode_token in app/auth.py). If deployed without overriding it, anyone who has read this source can forge access tokens for any user_id/role and fully bypass authentication.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The access_token session cookie is set with secure=False, so it will be transmitted over plain HTTP. Combined with httponly/samesite=lax this still allows the auth cookie to be captured via network interception on any non-TLS hop.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The SPA catch-all route joins the raw request path directly into a filesystem path (os.path.join(frontend_build, path)) and serves it with FileResponse whenever the resulting path exists as a file, with no normalization or containment check against frontend_build. A request path containing traversal sequences (e.g. /../../../etc/passwd or an absolute-looking segment) can cause the server to serve arbitrary files outside frontend_build.

cwe: CWE-22: Path Traversal

extra.message: get_job returns the full JobOut model (which includes internal_notes, an ops/dispatcher-only field) to any user who passes can_access_job, including customers viewing their own job. Internal dispatcher notes are disclosed to the customer role with no field filtering.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: get_incident (and list_incidents at lines 25-74) return the full IncidentOut model, including internal_notes and assigned_to, to customers. The code explicitly acknowledges this ('Pydantic will still include it; we rely on frontend to not display... for now, we'll trust the frontend') instead of stripping the fields server-side, so any customer can read internal incident handling notes for their own job's incidents via the API directly.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: export_incidents writes Incident.title (and other fields) directly into a CSV response without neutralizing leading =, +, -, @ characters. Incident title/description is attacker-controlled (any authenticated user, including a customer, can set it via POST /api/incidents/), so a crafted title such as "=cmd|'/c calc'!A1" becomes a formula-injection / CSV-injection payload that executes when an ops_admin opens the exported CSV in Excel.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: _wrk_gate compares the caller-supplied x-internal-token header to the secret gate_value with the != operator, which is not constant-time. This enables a timing side-channel to brute-force the internal ops token, and there is no rate limiting on repeated attempts.
